newsitem.title: USA: Tired Yeltsin misses G7 concert.
newsitem.headline: Tired Yeltsin misses G7 concert.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly missed a gala concert during the Group of Seven summit on Saturday and officials said he did not attend because he was tired.

Daniel Tarullo, deputy security affairs assistant to U.S. President Bill Clinton, said Yeltsin had left a summit dinner before the concert and returned to his hotel. "He was tired, he was just tired," Tarullo told reporters.
Yeltsin left the dinner about 20 minutes ahead of G7 leaders. Journalists had been told the leaders would all leave together.
A Kremlin official said: "He is in his residence, he decided that he would prefer not to take part in this event." But he added: "Tomorrow's meetings will go ahead according to plan."
A Russian delegation source said the president, who spent eight months out of office from the middle of last year after heart problems, surgery and pneumonia, was tired.

The concert had been included in the early schedules distributed by the Kremlin for the Russian president, and the organisers said they had expected him to join the G7 leaders from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.

Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year and he underwent quintuple bypass surgery on November 5. His recovery was interrupted by pneumonia in both lungs before he returned invigorated to the Kremlin and vowed to press on with a reformist policy.

Yeltsin, 66, had looked fit and trim at Friday's start of the three-day meeting, dubbed the Summit of the Eight to reflect Russia's more prominent role. He clearly enjoyed the limelight, wading into a crowd to shake hands and sitting next to U.S. President Bill Clinton during some of the events.
But he appeared tired during the summit's first full day on Saturday, when he attended the morning sessions and then met U.S. business leaders to urge them to invest in Russia.
The "mile-high" Denver summit was Yeltsin's first long excursion from Russia since he recovered from heart surgery, although he has made several trips within Russia and to other European countries.
White House press aide David Neslen said: "He was tired, he left the restaurant, he went to his hotel. That's the only thing we can say."
Police outside the hotel confirmed that Yeltsin had returned to his residence, but -- so far as they knew -- no doctor had been called.
Denver is more than 5,000 feet (1,550 metres) high in the foothills of the Rocky Mountains and visitors are warned to acclimatize gradually because of the debilitating effects of altitude.

Yeltsin has a long history of embarrassing disappearing acts, failing to show up for a meeting with Japan's foreign minister in 1992 and leaving Irish officials standing on the tarmac dring a stopover at Shannon airport in September 1994.
